name: Blackened Chicken with Mango Salsa
writer_notes: Primal Kitchen Avocado Lime Dipping Sauce appears in the source transcription as an optional 'if using' garnish but is NOT on the locked costed buy list; deliberately omitted from all steps to avoid an orphaned/unpurchased ingredient, and added to forbidden_prose_terms.
Source offered 'avocado oil' and 'orange juice' as alternatives; the build buys olive oil and lime juice, so only those two are written.
Olive oil is divided in the buy string (7 tbsp): about 1 tbsp goes into the salsa, the remainder cooks the chicken. Steps reference this without stating a computed split.
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes zero per-package price claims (only package-size references) and cost_closing uses the ${{cost_ps}} token instead of a literal.

REPAIR 2026-08-28: protein literal in intro_html, portion_html and head.description corrected from 43.6 g to the locked spec stat of 44 g per serving (Source-QA prose-numbers finding). Calories (620) were not flagged and stand. All macro figures in prose are locked engine values, transcribed not computed.

prose.intro_html:
Here is a dinner that tastes like a vacation and costs like a Tuesday. Blackened chicken brings the heat, a fresh mango salsa cools it right back down, and a bed of cilantro lime rice makes the whole thing stick to your ribs. That contrast is what keeps you out of the drive-thru line at six o'clock.

The numbers do the talking, and they are good numbers. Each of the 14 containers lands at 620 calories with 44 grams of protein, so this is a real meal that keeps you full instead of a sad little cup of lettuce. Spicy chicken, sweet mango, creamy avocado, all in one bowl you built with your own two hands.
prose.shop_smart:
Chicken breast is the anchor here at 5 1/4 pounds, so grab the biggest family pack you can find and cut it down yourself. Buying it in one big pack beats picking up a stack of shrink-wrapped single trays.

This build leans on produce that ripens on your counter, so time it right. You want 3 1/2 large mangoes and 3 1/2 large avocados that give a little when you press them, not rocks and not mush. If the store only has firm ones, buy a couple days ahead and let them come around before batch day.

Cilantro shows up in two different spots, but only the 3 1/2 fresh bunches go into the salsa. The frozen rice already carries its own cilantro and lime, so do not double buy. Seven 10 ounce bags of frozen cilantro lime rice handle the whole base and cook straight from the freezer.

A jar of blackened seasoning covers the 6 tablespoons this batch needs with plenty left for next time, and about 2 limes give you all the juice the salsa wants. Round it out with the red onion and the olive oil you already keep in the pantry.
prose.make_it:
Start with the salsa so the flavors have time to get friendly. Dice the mango and the avocado, chop the cilantro, and mince the red onion, then add them all to a large bowl. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, pour in about a tablespoon of the olive oil and the fresh lime juice, and toss until everything is coated. Set it aside.

Now the chicken. Dice the 5 1/4 pounds of breast into 1 inch cubes and toss with the blackened seasoning until every piece is coated. Get a large cast iron skillet hot over medium-high heat and add the rest of your olive oil. Work in batches so you do not crowd the pan, and sear the chicken about 3 minutes per side until it is no longer pink in the center and reaches 165 degrees. Let it rest while you finish the base.

Cook the frozen cilantro lime rice right on the package instructions. Seven bags is a lot to move at once, so run them in rounds and hold them warm. That is your bed for every bowl.
prose.portion_html:
This makes 14 containers, and the honest way to split it even is to weigh it, not eyeball it. Cook everything, set an empty container on the kitchen scale, and zero it out. Weigh your full pot of rice, divide by 14, and drop that same weight into each container. Do the exact same with the chicken. Eyeballing scoops is how the first few boxes get robbed and the last one shows up half empty.

Spoon the mango salsa over the top of each bowl, or pack it on the side if you like it bright and fresh come lunchtime. Either way, every container comes out to the same 620 calories and 44 grams of protein, no favorites at this table.
prose.cost_closing_html:
All in, this whole spread comes to ${{cost_ps}} per container. That is a spicy, fresh, protein-packed dinner for less than what a single fast food combo runs you, and you walked out with 14 of them.

Run the math on your week. Fourteen dinners at ${{cost_ps}} apiece is the kind of grocery trip that quietly pays you back, and you never once had to wonder what was actually in your food.

head.description: Blackened chicken with fresh mango salsa over cilantro lime rice. A budget meal-prep dinner that scales to 14 containers at 620 calories and 44g protein each.
head.keywords: blackened chicken, mango salsa, chicken meal prep, high protein dinner, cilantro lime rice, budget meal prep, meal prep bowls
steps: Make the mango salsa. Dice the mango and avocado, chop the cilantro, and mince the red onion, and add them to a large bowl. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, add about a tablespoon of the olive oil and the fresh lime juice, and toss until well combined. Set aside.
Season the chicken. Dice the chicken breast into 1 inch cubes and toss with the blackened seasoning until every piece is evenly coated.

Sear the chicken. Heat the rest of the olive oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Working in batches so the pan is not crowded, cook the chicken about 3 minutes per side until it is no longer pink in the center and reaches 165 degrees. Let it rest.
Cook the cilantro lime rice. Prepare the frozen cilantro lime rice bags according to the package instructions, running them in rounds since it is a large batch.
Build the containers. Divide the rice and chicken evenly across 14 containers by weight, then top each with the mango salsa or pack it on the side.
